title: the Mandukya Karika (Gaudapada)
hook: the chicken or the egg? Gaudapada takes the old seed-and-sprout puzzle somewhere nobody at the dinner table expects

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Mandukya Karika and the rope in the dark: the snake never went anywhere, because it was never apart from the rope. Rope or snake, what startled you? Day one thousand two hundred forty.

The argument starts over dessert. Which came first, the chicken or the egg? Somebody says the chicken, obviously, something had to lay it. Somebody else says the egg, obviously, the chicken hatched from one. A cousin brings up evolution. An uncle says it's a trick question. Nobody wins, and everybody has a good time. Thinkers in India argued over the same kind of loop, with a seed and a sprout: the seed makes the sprout, the sprout makes the seed. Gaudapada picks up that puzzle in the Mandukya Karika. But he doesn't pick a side. He asks whether anything was ever really born at all. Today: a daring word.
screen: `THE CHICKEN OR THE EGG?` → `SEED AND SPROUT.` → `WAS ANYTHING EVER BORN?`

segments.voice: The word is ajati. Jati means birth. A-jati means no birth, non-origination. It's a teaching that runs underneath the Karika. Here's how Gaudapada gets there. Try to explain how something comes to be. Does it come from something that already exists? Then it didn't really come to be; it was already there. Does it come from what doesn't exist at all? Nothing comes from nothing. Cause and effect chasing each other, like seed and sprout, never find a first beginning. So, he says, the wise don't affirm birth. Then he puts it in a stark verse. There is no dissolution and no origination. No one bound, no one striving, no one seeking freedom, no one freed. That, he says, is the highest truth. It can sound cold the first time. No one freed? After all this seeking? But look at it from yesterday's path. When the rope is seen, the snake isn't killed. Nothing is destroyed, nothing is saved. You simply see that the danger was never born. Gaudapada also says why the scriptures describe creation at all: stories of the world coming forth, like sparks from a fire or pots from clay, are a way of leading the mind toward the truth, not the last word on it. That's a bold claim, and it's his. Some other Vedanta schools hold that creation is real and that the Lord truly brings the world forth, and they answer him with care. Ajati is the deep end of Gaudapada's pool.
screen: `AJATI: NO BIRTH.` · `NOT FROM BEING, NOT FROM NOTHING.` · `NO ONE BOUND, NO ONE FREED.` · `CREATION STORIES LEAD THE MIND.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: watch a thought arrive, and look for where it began. Settle, and let the mind be as it is. When a thought appears, a plan, a memory, a tune, gently ask: where did it start? Don't chase an answer. Just look for its first moment. Then let it go, and wait for the next one. If you pray, you can rest in what was here before any thought. The bell holds the time.
The Mandukya Karika. Gaudapada's verses on the Mandukya Upanishad, carrying his teaching of ajati: on his reading, nothing at all is ever truly born. Today's word.
Your line: the Mandukya Karika, Gaudapada. Today, when a worry shows up fully formed, ask it gently: when exactly were you born? Day one thousand two hundred forty.

howItsDone: Students of Advaita Vedanta meet Gaudapada's teaching of ajati by reading the Karika, often with a teacher and with Shankara's commentary.

fork.setup: the chicken or the egg, the seed or the sprout. you're Gaudapada. how do you answer?
options: ask whether anything was ever truly born.
fork.reveal: he follows cause and effect until no first beginning can be found, and teaches ajati, no birth.

original.note: Sanskrit: no birth, non-origination; Gaudapada's teaching that nothing is truly born.

trapdoor: what you thought: ajati means the world is fake and nothing matters.
what it means: Gaudapada says nothing is truly born, so there is nothing to destroy and no one truly bound.
what a scholar hears: Mandukya Karika 2.32, no dissolution, no origination, none bound, none freed, called the highest truth.
recall: stilling the movements of the mind
the year just walked and kept

sources.ref: Mandukya Karika 2.32 (no dissolution, no origination, none bound, none striving, none seeking liberation, none liberated: the highest truth)
Mandukya Karika 3.15 (creation taught through clay, iron, sparks and the like as a means of leading the mind)
Mandukya Karika 4.3–4.4 and 4.14–4.23 (nothing born from the existent or the non-existent; the wise do not affirm birth; cause and effect, seed and sprout, without a first beginning)

notes: Ajati is presented as Gaudapada's teaching and as 'the deep end' within Advaita, not as a claim for all Hindus.

Confirm verse references: 2.32 (no dissolution, no origination...), 3.15 (creation through clay, iron, sparks as a means), and the seed/sprout and existent/non-existent arguments in chapter 4 (around 4.3–4.4, 4.14–4.23). Exact verse numbers are approximate in the fourth source.
'Pots from clay' and 'sparks from a fire' stand for the Karika's list of creation illustrations; confirm.
The chicken-and-egg hook is modern; the seed-and-sprout loop is the Karika's.
Original ajati: confirm Devanagari and stress.

Editor pass: 'the teaching that runs underneath the whole Karika' softened to 'a teaching'; 'other Vedanta schools' to 'some other'; 'within Advaita, ajati is treated as' (an unsourced claim about the school) trimmed.
